gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the same defect: the density and whole-line regularity arguments invoke a global L²(R,H) weak-solution definition for a nonzero homogeneous evolution that is only locally square-integrable. It also identifies the resulting invalid density justification and supplies the L²_loc repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The whole-line extension e^{-itH}u0 has constant nonzero norm, so it is not in the stated global L²(R,H) solution class; consequently the extension-based density and related whole-line argument are unjustified.

component_coverage.gold_component: The old global L²(R,H) weak-solution definition is incompatible with the nonzero homogeneous whole-line extension used in the density proof and whole-line regularity theorem, invalidating the associated extension-based arguments.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states the global L² requirement, gives the constant-norm nonzero homogeneous extension as a counterexample, identifies its incompatible use in both density and whole-line regularity, and proposes the matching L²_loc repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns an incorrect time-horizon dependence in norm and coercivity estimates. It does not identify the distinct spectral-cutoff proof error in which the time-mollified residual rho_n*(1_I f) is incorrectly identified with the spectral-projection residual, nor does it address the resulting missing convergence in X_H.
